Schedule 1hr technical deep dive for private deployment with Aurelia infra team (week of 5/25)
Provide sample log retention/redaction options and config examples
action_items: Ethan Park: Email SOC2 + HIPAA checklist and network diagram (due 2026-05-15)
Maya Singh: Prepare rough performance cost model for 50 req/s with typical clinical prompt sizes (due 2026-05-18)
Jamal Ortiz: Share current infra diagram and list of connected PHI databases (due 2026-05-20)

summary: Discovery call focused on whether Aurelia should use Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, or Private. Main concerns were PHI handling, EU patient data (GDPR), log retention and redaction, KMS key residency, and network isolation. Customer leans towards Dedicated or Private for sensitive workloads but wants cost/latency tradeoffs and evidence of audit controls before committing.
topics: Log retention, redaction, and audit trails
Hosting options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
questions: Can Redwood ensure PHI never leaves customer region for specific routes?
How does Redwood handle encryption keys and can keys be customer-managed (HSM/KMS)?
What are options for removing sensitive payloads from logs or sending only metadata to Redwood Console?
If we use Dedicated, do we get tenant-level isolation and dedicated GPU pools?
What's the fallback behavior if Dedicated capacity is exhausted?
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park, Maya Singh, Liam O'Connor (Redwood); Dr. Lena Morales, Jamal Ortiz, Priya Nambiar, Tao Chen (Aurelia)

[00:00] Ethan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for taking time today. Quick intros — I'm Ethan, AE at Redwood, Maya is our infra SE, Liam is with solutions. How are you all?
[00:12] Dr. Lena Morales: Doing well, thanks. We've got a lot to cover around HIPAA and eur... GDPR overlap so appreciate you fitting us in.
[00:22] Jamal Ortiz: Hi all, Jamal here — lead platform. We'll want to understand hosting options and what the traffic footprint looks like.
[00:30] Maya Singh: Great, quick agenda — collect compliance requirements, discuss hosting options (hosted/dedicated/private), KMS and key residency, logging/redaction, and then identify next steps. Sound good?
[00:42] Priya Nambiar: Yep. Primary ask: we have PHI in some pipelines so we need either assurance that PHI is never logged or the ability to scrub it before ingestion. Also region restrictions for EU patients.
[00:54] Liam O'Connor: Absolutely. To set expectations, Redwood has three common deployment paths: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools, tenant isolation), and Private (VPC or on-prem for full control). We can run through how each handles keys, logs, and residency.
[01:10] Dr. Lena Morales: When you say "tenant isolation" for Dedicated, is that logical or physical? We need to know for audit.
[01:18] Maya Singh: Dedicated is isolated compute — dedicated pools so your workload won't share the same GPU hosts as other customers. Network-wise we provide isolated subnets and egress controls, but it's still managed by Redwood control plane unless you take Private.
[01:34] Tao Chen: So for Private we'd manage the control plane? Or is it a customer-managed control plane on our infra?
[01:40] Liam O'Connor: For Private we offer two models: VPC-private control plane (control plane in our infra but reachable over private link/VPN) or fully on-prem where you run Redwood components yourself. On-prem gives you full network isolation and lets you keep keys on your HSM.
[01:56] Jamal Ortiz: Okay, good. For GDPR: we have EU patient data and want to ensure processing doesn't leave EU. Is there region locking?
[02:04] Ethan Park: Yes, we have region pinning for models and endpoints — you can route EU data to our EU-hosted Dedicated or Private deployment. We can also configure automatic geofence fallback but we would want to avoid that if policy forbids cross-border processing.
[02:20] Priya Nambiar: What's the evidence we can provide for auditors? Specifics like logs showing ingress region and retention controls, plus SOC 2 and HIPAA attestation docs.
[02:29] Maya Singh: We'll share SOC 2 report and our HIPAA BAAs. For logs, Redwood Console stores request metadata and token accounting; however by default some transit logs are kept for a configurable retention. You can opt to disable storing request payloads and only keep metadata. We also support log redaction hooks — either pre-ingest hooks at your edge that scrub PHI, or server-side redaction rules.
[02:50] Dr. Lena Morales: Server-side redaction is interesting but auditors like proof that ingestion can be prevented in the first place. Can we show an exec summary for both approaches?
[02:58] Ethan Park: Yes — we'll send a short matrix showing pre-ingest scrubbing vs server-side redaction vs no-logs routing. We'll also note tradeoffs: pre-ingest gives strongest assurance but adds latency and engineering work, server-side redaction is easier but requires trust in the redaction pipeline.
[03:16] Tao Chen: On encryption: keys — we require customer-managed keys for any PHI processing. Does Redwood allow HSM-backed keys with geofencing?
[03:24] Liam O'Connor: We support customer KMS integration and can bind keys to region-specific providers. For Private on-prem, you can use your HSM; for Dedicated we can integrate with your cloud KMS and restrict key usage to certain regions. There are some integration patterns to discuss.
[03:40] Priya Nambiar: If we use Redwood Hosted for non-PHI workloads but Dedicated for PHI, can we have separate routing rules by route name or API key?
[03:49] Maya Singh: Yes, routing is policy-driven. You can route based on API key, model, or request attributes. Many customers keep low-risk traffic on Hosted and route PHI to Dedicated or Private. There is an overhead for Dedicated (cost) but you get predictable throughput.
[04:06] Jamal Ortiz: Cost stacks matter. For Dedicated, if we need burst capacity and Dedicated pool is saturated, what's Redwood's fallback?
[04:13] Ethan Park: Fallback options can be configured — you can set hard fail, queue, or fallback to a lower-cost but compatible model in a different capacity tier. For PHI routes, many customers choose hard fail or queuing rather than cross-region fallback.
[04:30] Dr. Lena Morales: We need SLOs too — latency guarantees for triage flows versus async batch.
[04:36] Maya Singh: We can supply SLOs for Dedicated with SLA credits. Hosted is best-effort with published performance profiles but no hard SLA at lower tiers. We also have observability to show token-level latencies and per-route dashboards.
[04:52] Jamal Ortiz: About logs: can we redact parts of the request and still retain enough trace to debug? Example: remove PHI but keep prompt hash and timing metadata.
[05:00] Liam O'Connor: Yep — common pattern is to hash the prompt, store hashes plus non-sensitive metadata, and remove or mask entities recognized as PHI. We can show examples of redaction rules and console screenshots.
[05:15] Dr. Lena Morales: Any concerns about model cache (KV cache) leaking PHI?
[05:21] Maya Singh: Good callout. The KV cache is per-model and per-host. For PHI routes you'd want to ensure caching is disabled or that KV cache isn't persisted across requests — we support ephemeral KV caches for sensitive workloads. Sometimes the transcript spells it "kay-vee cache" in notes but it's the same thing.
[05:38] Priya Nambiar: Auditors ask about retention timelines. Do you have configurable retention windows for logs and traces?
[05:44] Ethan Park: Yes — retention is configurable from 0 days up to several years depending on plan. For Dedicated and Private we can support custom retention policies and provide export for offline archival or deletion.
[05:56] Tao Chen: For private deployment, what does the upgrade path look like? We don't want to be stuck on old kernel versions and lose features.
[06:03] Liam O'Connor: Private on-prem includes a supported upgrade cadence; Redwood releases quarterly patches and we can coordinate staged rollouts. If you run the on-prem fully-managed bundle you get the updates via our release channel; if you self-host we provide the upgrade artifact and runbook.
[06:20] Jamal Ortiz: Any requirements for network egress? Our security team wants to lock down egress and only allow certain IPs.
[06:27] Maya Singh: For Dedicated we can restrict egress to set IP ranges and set up private link. Private on-prem gives you full control. Hosted requires more relaxed egress policies since control plane interactions occur.
[06:40] Dr. Lena Morales: Does Redwood have any HIPAA breaches in their history? Auditors will ask.
[06:45] Ethan Park: No known HIPAA breaches. We'll surface our compliance history in the SOC2/HIPAA materials.
[06:52] Priya Nambiar: We also need to know what data is included in your support tickets and debugging sessions. We don't want PHI in case of a support case.
[07:00] Liam O'Connor: Support workflows can be configured to strip request payloads for sensitive routes. For Dedicated we can set support access to metadata-only and require a signed NDA for full payload access. For Private, you control support artifacts.
[07:16] Jamal Ortiz: Can we get a POC with sample throughput? Maybe a 2-week pilot where we send synthetic PHI traffic into a Dedicated pool?
[07:25] Maya Singh: Absolutely — typical pilots run 2–4 weeks. We'll need a scope: endpoints, target QPS, model size, and logging/regulatory constraints. We'll give a rough cost estimate for a pilot.
[07:38] Dr. Lena Morales: For GDPR, who is the data controller vs processor? How does Redwood present that relationship?
[07:46] Ethan Park: Redwood is typically a processor and you (Aurelia) are the controller. We can include standard processor terms and any additional DPA clauses. For Private on-prem it behaves more like a contracted software where you're operating the processing within your boundary.
[08:00] Priya Nambiar: On legal holds: we occasionally need to preserve data for litigation. Is there an environment for producing raw logs when needed?
[08:07] Liam O'Connor: Yes — we support legal hold exports. For Dedicated/Private we can provide an immutable export snapshot for the hold period. For Hosted we'll need to coordinate and we can provide exports per agreement.
[08:22] Jamal Ortiz: Anything else we should know about model variant and quantization recommendations for sensitive workloads?
[08:28] Maya Singh: We recommend smaller quantized variants for cost but validate quality. For PHI-sensitive workloads customers often pick a stable model pin with a rollback plan. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles by workload to balance latency, cost and quality.
[08:44] Dr. Lena Morales: One concern — if we tokenize PHI differently across languages, does Redwood provide any language-specific redaction templates?
[08:52] Ethan Park: We have language-aware entity recognition as part of redaction rules, though it's not perfect. For high-assurance needs, pre-ingest scrubbing is the gold standard. We'll include examples for major EU languages.
[09:05] Priya Nambiar: Could you walk through a concrete example: patient note goes in, how do we prevent PHI from showing up in SRE logs and the console?
[09:13] Liam O'Connor: Sure: 1) route note to PHI-dedicated endpoint, 2) enable payload-blocking in the ingestion pipeline, 3) enable redaction rules to mask patient identifiers, 4) configure console to only retain prompt hash + timing metadata, not full payload, 5) bind a customer-managed KMS key for any stored artifacts. We'll provide a flow diagram.
[09:38] Dr. Lena Morales: That helps. Auditors will ask for screenshots and evidence.
[09:42] Maya Singh: We'll attach sample config and screenshots with the redaction toggles and the retention policy UI.
[09:49] Jamal Ortiz: For the pilot, we want to validate encryption in transit and at rest, plus key rotation. How long to set up a Dedicated pilot?
[09:56] Ethan Park: Typically 2–3 weeks to provision Dedicated with baseline configs; quicker if we have network details and KMS access. Private on-prem takes longer (4–8 weeks) depending on infra.
[10:08] Priya Nambiar: One last auditor-y question: do you provide proof of deletion when we ask for data erasure?
[10:14] Liam O'Connor: Yes — for Dedicated/Private we can provide deletion certificates and export logs showing purged objects. For Hosted we'll coordinate and provide deletion evidence per the DPA.
[10:27] Dr. Lena Morales: Are there any incompatibilities with our existing stack? We run in GCP and use their KMS and private interconnect.
[10:34] Maya Singh: We integrate with GCP KMS and private interconnect. We'll want Jamal's infra diagram and an IP allowlist.
[10:43] Jamal Ortiz: I'll share that after the call.
[10:46] Ethan Park: Great. Quick recap — we heard three must-haves: customer-managed keys, log redaction/no-payload storage for PHI routes, and region locking for EU data. You prefer Dedicated for PHI, Hosted for non-PHI. Pilot scope to validate encryption/key rotation and retention/export.
[11:06] Priya Nambiar: Correct. Also need the SOC2/HIPAA docset and a short matrix of tradeoffs.
[11:12] Ethan Park: We'll send those. Maya, any technical items we should call out?
[11:16] Maya Singh: I'll prepare a performance vs cost estimate for 50 req/s with clinical prompt sizes and outline redaction options. Also will include sample ingestion flow diagrams and log retention configs.
[11:28] Dr. Lena Morales: Next step — schedule the deep dive (week of 5/25) and please include your private deployment engineer if possible.
[11:36] Liam O'Connor: Yep — can do. We'll send calendar invites.
[11:40] Jamal Ortiz: Thanks everyone.
[11:42] Ethan Park: Thanks — we'll follow up with materials tomorrow.
[11:46] End of recording.

Notes on transcription: some words auto-corrected (e.g., "kay-vee" for KV cache), occasional overlap and filler words removed for readability.
recording_notes: Transcript contains typical ASR idiosyncrasies: some proper nouns mis-recognized, occasional dropped connectors. Customers requested redaction examples and SOC2/HIPAA materials. Pilot requested for Dedicated path to validate PHI handling.
